summary.goal: Build an adaptive learning loop that observes Forge execution outcomes and ideation session quality, builds performance baselines, detects drift, and learns optimal configuration via Thompson sampling. Produces ForgeExecutionConfig, PlannerConfig, and IdeationConfig. CLI-only interface for operators.
in_scope: Outcome collection from Forge (task + run outcomes)
Outcome collection from Ideation (session outcomes on handoff)
Plan quality signal collection from Planner (on approval of ideation-sourced plans)
Baseline computation for task patterns and ideation quality
Drift detection (duration, tokens, success rate, ideation metrics)
Config generation for Forge, Planner, and Ideation
Ideation config: interviewer model, confidence calibration, specialist spawning rules, readiness advisory
Stability controls for all config changes (burn-in, min samples, hysteresis, rate limiting, credible intervals)
SQLite storage for outcomes, baselines, config versions
REST API for config read / outcome write
CLI for status, config, override, history
out_of_scope: A/B testing for Interviewer model (conversation quality is too subjective for binary signal)
Per-topic ideation baselines (single 'session_quality' pattern for v1, per-topic requires volume)
Keyword correlation tracking for specialist spawn rules (defer to later)
Gating ideation handoff (readiness advisory is informational only, never blocking)
Assessing conversation quality or block correctness (subjective, user's job via curation)
Human feedback metrics (goal achievement, user satisfaction) - these require user input, Tuner is automated-only
Planning-time guardrails (missing security, incomplete scope) - these belong in Planner, not Tuner
Subjective quality assessment - Tuner measures pass/fail, not 'is this good code'

acceptance_criteria.description: Forge can read ForgeExecutionConfig from /api/tuner/config/forge
Planner can read PlannerConfig from /api/tuner/config/planner
Ideation can read IdeationConfig from /api/tuner/config/ideation
Forge can POST TaskOutcome to /api/tuner/outcomes/task
Forge can POST RunOutcome to /api/tuner/outcomes/run
Ideation can POST IdeationOutcome to /api/tuner/outcomes/ideation
Planner can POST PlanQualitySignal to /api/tuner/outcomes/plan-quality
Baselines are computed with exponential moving average after minimum samples
Drift alerts are generated when metrics exceed 2σ from baseline
Model selection uses Thompson sampling with 10% initial exploration rate
Exploration rate decays as sample count grows
Ideation config changes use same stability controls as Forge/Planner (burn-in=50, min samples=30, CI width≤0.10, 24h default cool-down)
IdeationConfig defaults match current hardcoded values (day-one behavior identical)
Ideation works identically when Tuner is unreachable (graceful fallback)
CLI shows current baselines and active drift alerts
Config versions are stored with audit trail
All storage operations use SQLite with proper indexes

observations: Algorithms are mathematical with known correct outputs - easy to verify
Cold start is critical path - system must work with no prior data
Verification fields are new - need explicit coverage
TunerClient graceful degradation is important for Forge resilience
concerns: Thompson sampling is probabilistic - tests need statistical assertions (e.g., over 1000 trials)
Time-based tests (rate limiting) may be flaky - use dependency injection for clock

tester.mocking: In-memory storage for unit tests, temp SQLite for integration

patterns.statistical_tests: Run N trials, assert ratio is within expected range (e.g., 60-80%)
patterns.time_tests: Inject clock/timer to avoid real delays

summary.goal: Learn optimal model selection using Thompson sampling multi-armed bandit with stability controls

acceptance_criteria.description: selectModel checks hard rules first (from config)
Random model selected with probability = exploration_rate (during burn-in)
Thompson sampling samples from Beta(α,β) for each model
Model with highest sampled value is selected (after passing stability checks)
recordOutcome updates Beta distribution (α++ on success, β++ on failure)
New model/taskType/complexity starts with Beta(1,1) prior
sampleBeta uses Gamma distribution sampling trick
MIN_SAMPLES (30) required per arm before exploitation (use round-robin during burn-in)
Hysteresis: new model must have ≥15% higher probability than current to switch

summary.goal: Prevent parameter flapping with insufficient data using burn-in, rate limiting, hysteresis, and credible interval checks

acceptance_criteria.description: BURN_IN_TRIALS (50) enforces round-robin during initial exploration
MIN_SAMPLES_PER_ARM (30) required before Thompson sampling exploitation
Rate limiting: config changes limited to once per COOL_DOWN_PERIOD (1 hour for model selection)
Hysteresis: IMPROVEMENT_MARGIN (15%) required before parameter switch
Credible interval check: 95% CI width must be < 0.10 before acting
StabilityConfig type with all thresholds (burn_in_trials, min_samples_per_arm, cool_down_ms, improvement_margin, max_ci_width)

plan_tests.strategy: Algorithm correctness first, then API contracts, then error handling

cases.description: EMA converges: 10 samples at value=100 → mean approaches 100
Welford stddev: known values [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9] → stddev ≈ 2.0
First sample: initializes with stddev=0, sample_count=1
Cold start: getBaseline returns null for unknown pattern
Verification rate: tracks percentage of tasks with all verifications passing
No alert when within 1σ of baseline
Warning at exactly 2σ deviation
Critical at exactly 3σ deviation
Skip detection when sample_count < 30
Skip detection when stddev = 0 (avoid division by zero)
Hard rule match: complexity=trivial → haiku
Thompson sampling: model with higher α/(α+β) selected more often
